# Isaiah Chapter 45 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 153r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/ISA_045_page_001.jpg

---

**45:1** Thus says YHWH to his-anointed [li-meshicho], to-Koresh [Cyrus], whom-I-have-grasped [hechezaqti] by-his-right-hand [bi-ymino] to-subdue [le-rad] before-him nations [goyim], and-the-loins [motnei] of-kings [melakhim] I-will-loose [efatteach]; to-open [liftoach] before-him doors [delatayim] and-gates [u-she'arim] will-not be-shut [lo yissageru]:

**45:7** "I-form [yotser] light [or] and-create [u-vorei] darkness [choshekh]; I-make [oseh] peace [shalom] and-create [u-vorei] evil [ra]; I, YHWH, do [oseh] all these [kol-elleh]."

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — "his anointed... Cyrus":** The most shocking verse in Second Isaiah. *Mashiach* ("anointed one/messiah") applied to a Persian pagan king. Cyrus conquered Babylon in 539 BCE and permitted the Jews to return. For Isaiah, Cyrus is YHWH's instrument — chosen without knowing YHWH.

**v.7 — "I form light and create darkness":** Often cited in debates about theodicy. YHWH claims authorship of both *shalom* (peace/well-being) and *ra* (evil/calamity). Whether *ra* means moral evil or natural disaster is debated; the theological claim is that YHWH is sovereign over all reality.

*— EMET*
